what_happened: The job to find and remove the cause of the longer producer stage (12.7 to 23.5 minutes) was rejected at the final verdict. Two of 5 acceptance criteria were unmet. First, the design note under docs/design/ did not give a correct cause with cited code paths and measured numbers. Second, the fix did not remove the real cause, and the note did not say what the next throughput review should show. There were three blocker or major findings. The blocker: the stated root cause is contradicted by the recorded producer timings, so it was inferred from code and dates when the records could have been read. One major finding: the note gives the wrong date for the previous throughput review and says no records were available. Another major finding: the claim that the command forces a cold build of most of the workspace on every job is overstated. No checks failed.
cause: A diagnosis job has no step that makes the producer read the recorded evidence (per-job stage timings, earlier review dates) before it names a cause. Nothing requires a root-cause claim to be tested against those records. The criteria asked only for a note that cites numbers and labels estimates, so a note built from code reading and dates passed until the verifier compared it with the records. The class chosen is a loose fit: the registry has no class for a diagnosis written from inference when records were available, and 20261026-061735-8rvt (a doc written without surveying existing material, caught only at the final verdict) is the closest.
prevention: For jobs that diagnose a regression, split the job in two. First, a measuring step produces a table from the recorded per-job stage timings: median producer time by date, and the change points. The table is committed. Second, the cause and the fix may only name a change that matches a change point in that table, and the note must cite the table. A code check should refuse a diagnosis note that has no timings table drawn from the records, or that cites a date not found in them.
proposed_request: Find and remove the cause of the longer producer stage (median rose from about 12.7 to 23.5 minutes). Do it in this order. 1) Read the recorded per-job stage timings and write a table to docs/design/producer-slowdown.md: producer-stage duration per job by date, the median before and after, and the date where it changes. Take the previous throughput review date from the records, not from memory. 2) Name the cause only if it matches a change point in that table. Cite the code paths and the measured numbers. Label any estimate, and say how much of the rise the cause explains, without overstating it (do not claim a cold build of most of the workspace unless a recorded build time shows it). 3) Remove the cause itself in code or config. Do not raise a timeout or hide timing. 4) In the note, state what the next throughput review should show: a lower producer median, with the expected range. Acceptance: the note holds the timings table from the records; the stated cause matches the table; the previous review date matches the records; the fix changes the cause itself; the note states the expected lower producer median.
